summary: A complete target-level design of the dyadic unitary and symplectic ordinary lifting theorems of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni §§5–6: polarized deformation problems over a weight algebra at p = 2 with Taylor–Wiles presentations over Λ, Thorne's complex with h³ = 1, near adequacy and the unavoidable dual Selmer class (OL.0); ordinary Hecke algebras of definite unitary groups at p = 2 with Hida control (OL.1); the ordinary global problem, its dimension bound, the Hecke-valued Galois representation and sufficiently deep levels (OL.2); Theorem 5.7.14 through solvable preparation, ring–module patching over a weight algebra with torsion, two-type patching, the component structure, Ihara-avoidance support and removal of the auxiliary place (OL.3); GSp₄ problems over a weight algebra, GSp₄-reasonable images with their Taylor–Wiles places, seed data, the selected problem and the Hida–Hecke Galois representation (OL.4); and Theorem 6.3.4 through component dominance and patching (OL.5). Generic deformation theory, local ordinary rings, patching algebra and the l-odd unitary theory are imported; nothing is claimed formalised.

nodes.title: Polarized deformation problems up to Ĝ_n-conjugacy
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ₂ be finite with ring of integers O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field k. Let F be an imaginary CM field such that F/F⁺ is unramified at every finite place and every place of F⁺ above 2 splits in F. Let S be a finite set of places of F⁺ containing S_2 and S_∞, and let G_{F⁺,S} ⊃ G_{F,S} be the Galois groups of the maximal extension F(S) of F unramified outside S. Fix a continuous r̄ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(k) with r̄^{−1}(𝒢_n^0(k)) = G_{F,S} whose restriction ρ̄ to G_{F,S}, projected to GL_n, is absolutely irreducible, and a continuous χ : G_{F⁺,S} → O^× lifting ν ∘ r̄ with χ(c_v) = −1 for every v ∈ S_∞. For each v ∈ S fix Λ_v ∈ CNL_O and put Λ = ⊗̂_{v∈S} Λ_v. Define a lifting of r̄|G_{F⁺_v} to A ∈ CNL_{Λ_v} as a continuous r_v : G_{F⁺_v} → 𝒢_n(A) reducing to r̄|G_{F⁺_v} with ν ∘ r_v = χ|G_{F⁺_v}; the functor Lift^□_v is represented by R^□_v ∈ CNL_{Λ_v}. A local deformation problem D_v ⊂ Lift^□_v is a representable subfunctor stable under conjugation by Ĝ_n(A). A global deformation problem is a tuple 𝒮 = (F, r̄, O, χ, S, {Λ_v}_{v∈S}, {D_v}_{v∈S}). A lift of r̄ to A ∈ CNL_Λ is a continuous r : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(A) reducing to r̄ with ν ∘ r = χ; it is of type 𝒮 if r|G_{F⁺_v} ∈ D_v(A) for every v ∈ S. Two lifts are strictly equivalent if they are conjugate by an element of Ĝ_n(A), the whole kernel including its GL_1 factor. For T ⊂ S a T-framed lift of type 𝒮 is (r, (α_v)_{v∈T}) with α_v ∈ Ĝ_n(A), and (r, (α_v)) ~ (a r a^{−1}, (a α_v)) for a ∈ Ĝ_n(A). Def_𝒮 and Def^T_𝒮 : CNL_Λ → Set are the functors of strict equivalence classes of lifts, resp. T-framed lifts, of type 𝒮. When Λ_v = O for v ∈ S ∖ T, put R^loc_{𝒮,T} = ⊗̂_{v∈T} R_v, a Λ-algebra through ⊗̂_{v∈T} Λ_v ≅ Λ (BCGP25 §5.4, pp. 121–122; BCGP25 Lemma 5.1.2 and Remark 5.1.3, pp. 115–116).
acceptance: For T = ∅ the framed ring is R_𝒮 itself, and the framing torsor is the trivial group.
For n = 4 and #T = 3 the relative dimension of R^T_𝒮 over R_𝒮 is (16 + 1)·3 − 1 = 50; the GL_n-framing count n²#T − 1 = 47 omits the GL_1 factor of Ĝ_n and is wrong.

For γ = (B, b)j ∈ 𝒢_n(A) ∖ 𝒢_n^0(A) and a ∈ 1 + m_A, conjugation by (1, a) sends γ to (a^{−1}B, b)j and fixes 𝒢_n^0(A) pointwise; over A = k[ε] with p = 2 and a = 1 + ε, a is not a square ((x + yε)² = x²), so this conjugation is not induced by a scalar matrix.

For p = 2, n even and r̄(c_v) GL_n(k)-conjugate to (1_n, 1)j at a real place v, the functor of lifts up to 1 + M_n(m_A)-conjugacy differs from Def_𝒮: the one-dimensional µ_v of 1.2 is identified to zero by Ĝ_n-conjugacy and not by GL_n-conjugacy.

nodes.title: Thorne's complex, the dyadic dual Selmer group and Taylor–Wiles presentations over Λ
nodes.statement:
Keep the data of 1.1 with p = 2, let ad r̄ = M_n(k) = Lie GL_n ⊂ 𝔤_n r̄ = Lie 𝒢_n with the adjoint action of G_{F⁺,S} through r̄, so that 0 → ad r̄ → 𝔤_n r̄ → k → 0 is exact, and let L_v ⊂ H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄) be the image of the tangent space of D_v. The classes µ_v = ker(H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄) → H¹(F⁺_v, 𝔤_n r̄)) and the dual Selmer group H¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} ⊂ H¹(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄(1)), cut out by µ_v^⊥ at v ∈ T and by L_v^⊥ at v ∈ S ∖ T, are those of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.3, *Taylor–Wiles data when F contains ζ_p, including p = 2*; they depend only on the residual data, so they are the same for the Λ-coefficient problem. Let C^•_{𝒮,T} be Thorne's complex and h^i_{𝒮,T} the dimensions of its cohomology. Prove the following (BCGP25 §5.4, (5.4.1)–(5.4.3), pp. 122–123, and Remark 5.4.4, pp. 123–124; Tho17 Lemmas 2.12, 2.13, 2.15 and 2.17, Corollary 2.14): 1. µ_v is the image of the connecting map H⁰(F⁺_v, k) → H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄), so dim_k µ_v ≤ 1; µ_v ⊂ L_v; µ_v = 0 if v splits in F. At a real place v, dim_k µ_v = 1 if r̄(c_v) is GL_n(k)-conjugate to (1_n, 1)j, and µ_v = 0 if n is even and r̄(c_v) is conjugate to (Ψ_n, 1)j, Ψ_n the antidiagonal matrix.
2. For T ≠ ∅: h⁰_{𝒮,T} = 0, h^i_{𝒮,T} = 0 for i ≥ 4, h²_{𝒮,T} = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T}, and h³_{𝒮,T} = h⁰(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄(1)) = 1. Moreover h¹_{𝒮,T} = dim_k m_{R^T_𝒮}/(m_{R^loc_{𝒮,T}}, m²_{R^T_𝒮}), whatever the coefficient rings Λ_v.
3. If S = T ⊔ Q ⊔ S_∞ with S_2 ⊂ T, D_v = Lift^□_v at v ∈ S_∞ and Q a Taylor–Wiles datum with #Q = q, the Euler characteristic is χ_{𝒮_Q,T} = 1 − #T − q + dn(n−1)/2.
4. (Taylor–Wiles presentation over Λ.) Assume (i) χ(c_v) = −1 and D_v = Lift^□_v for v ∈ S_∞; (ii) F = F⁺(√−1); (iii) if n is even, r̄(c_v) is GL_n(k)-conjugate to (1_n, 1)j for some v ∈ S_∞; (iv) ρ̄(G_F) is nearly adequate (1.3); and let T = S ∖ S_∞. Put q = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} − 1 and g = q + #T − 1 − dn(n−1)/2. Then for each N ≥ 1 there are Taylor–Wiles data (Q, (α_v)_{v∈Q}) of level N with #Q = q and a surjection of R^loc_{𝒮,T}-algebras, hence of Λ-algebras, R^loc_{𝒮,T}⟦X_1, …, X_g⟧ ↠ R^T_{𝒮_Q} (BCGP25 Proposition 5.5.6, p. 126).
5. (Comparison with conjugate self-dual Selmer groups.) Restriction gives an exact sequence 0 → H¹(F/F⁺, k) → H¹(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄) → H¹(F(S)/F, ad r̄)^{Gal(F/F⁺)} → H²(F/F⁺, k) → H²(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄), and the restriction map is surjective as soon as some real place v has r̄(c_v) conjugate to (1_n, 1)j (automatic for n odd; strong residual oddness for n even).
prerequisites: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.3 (*Taylor–Wiles data when F contains ζ_p, including p = 2*) and PL.4 (*Strong residual oddness at a real place (p = 2)*)
proofSteps: (1) is the long exact sequence of 0 → ad r̄ → 𝔤_n r̄ → k → 0, Ĝ_n-stability of D_v and Tho17 Lemma 2.17. (2) is Tho17 Lemma 2.15 by Poitou–Tate, with h⁰ = 0 because T ≠ ∅, h^i = 0 for i ≥ 4 because global and archimedean cohomology agree in degrees ≥ 3 (Tho17 line 390), and h³ = 1 because at p = 2 the element j acts on Lie GL_n by X ↦ −ᵗX = ᵗX, so the scalars 1_n are G_{F⁺}-invariant in ad r̄(1) while ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible. (3) is Tho17 Corollary 2.14 with ℓ¹_v = n(n+1)/2 at real places and n² + 1 at v ∈ Q. (4) is the argument of PL.3 with relaxed adequacy replaced by near adequacy through 1.3, the coefficient rings entering only through R^loc_{𝒮,T} (KT17 §4; BCGP25 §5.4). (5) is inflation–restriction with coefficients ad r̄ and (ad r̄)^{G_F} = k; surjectivity holds because H²(F/F⁺, k) ≅ Ĥ⁰(Gal(ℂ/ℝ), k) maps to Ĥ⁰(Gal(ℂ/ℝ), ad r̄) = (ad r̄)^{c_v}/(1 + c_v)ad r̄ by 1 ↦ 1_n, and writing r̄(c_v) = (B, 1)j with B symmetric, 1_n ∈ (1 + c_v)ad r̄ exactly when B is alternating.
acceptance: Euler count with the corrected h³: for n = 2, d = 2, #T = 3, q = 5 and h² = h¹_{𝒮_Q^⊥,T} = 1, h¹ = h² − h³ − χ = 1 − 1 − (1 − 3 − 5 + 2) = 5 = g; using h³ = 0 would give 6 = g + 1, one more generator than the presentation of (4) provides.
At a split place v ∈ T, µ_v = 0, so µ_v^⊥ is all of H¹(F⁺_v, ad r̄(1)) and v imposes no condition on H¹_{𝒮^⊥,T}.

At a real place with r̄(c_v) = (Ψ_2, 1)j (n = 2), B = Ψ_2 is alternating, the map H²(F/F⁺, k) → Ĥ⁰(Gal(ℂ/ℝ), ad r̄) is zero and µ_v = 0; with r̄(c_v) = (1_2, 1)j, 1_2 ∉ (1 + c_v)ad r̄ = {Y + ᵗY}, which consists of matrices with zero diagonal.
For p odd the same computation gives h³_{𝒮,T} = h⁰(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄(1)), which vanishes when ζ_p ∉ F; the value 1 is a feature of F = F⁺(√−1) ∋ ζ_2.

nodes.title: Weak adequacy with the full adjoint, and near adequacy
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite field, V a finite-dimensional k-vector space, ad = End_k(V), ad⁰ the trace-zero endomorphisms, H ⊂ GL(V) a subgroup with set of semisimple elements H^ss, and for g ∈ H^ss and α ∈ k̄ let e_{g,α} be the projection of V ⊗ k̄ onto the generalized α-eigenspace of g. Let U = {w ∈ ad ⊗ k̄ : tr(gw) = 0 for all g ∈ H^ss}. Prove that U = {w : tr(e_{g,α}w) = 0 for all g ∈ H^ss and α}, that U is an H-submodule of ad⁰ ⊗ k̄, and that the following are equivalent: (1) every simple k̄[H]-submodule W ⊂ ad ⊗ k̄ has σ ∈ H^ss and an eigenvalue α of σ with tr(e_{σ,α}W) ≠ 0; (3) ad is spanned over k by H^ss; (U) U = 0. Deduce that BCGP's nearly adequate subgroups (weakly adequate, H¹(H, k) = 0 and H¹(H, ad) = 0; BCGP25 Definition 5.3.3) are exactly the relaxed-adequate subgroups of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.4 when k contains the eigenvalues of the elements of H (BCGP25 Lemma 5.3.1 and proof, p. 120; Definitions 5.3.2–5.3.3 and Remark 5.3.4, pp. 120–121). The equivalence of the ad⁰ trace condition with spanning, and absolute irreducibility of weakly adequate subgroups, are ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §7.9 and are not repeated.
prerequisites: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.4 (*Adequacy relaxed to the vanishing of H¹(H, ad)*)
proofSteps: each e_{g,α} is a polynomial in g and g = Σ_α α e_{g,α} for semisimple g, which identifies the two descriptions of U; H-stability follows from tr(g·hwh^{−1}) = tr(h^{−1}gh·w) with h^{−1}gh ∈ H^ss; g = 1 gives U ⊂ ad⁰ ⊗ k̄; nondegeneracy of the trace form gives (3) ⇔ (U); and (1) says that U, an H-submodule, meets the socle of ad ⊗ k̄ trivially, hence (1) ⇔ (U).
acceptance: U always lies in ad⁰ ⊗ k̄, because 1 ∈ H^ss; for H = {1} ⊂ GL₂(k), U = ad⁰ ⊗ k̄ is three-dimensional and H is not weakly adequate.

GL₂(𝔽₂) ≅ S₃ acts absolutely irreducibly on 𝔽₂², but its semisimple elements are 1, A and A² with A of order 3 (the involutions are unipotent), spanning only 𝔽₂[A] ≅ 𝔽₄ of dimension 2 < 4; absolute irreducibility does not give weak adequacy, and (1) fails for the simple submodule U ≠ 0.

A₅ ≅ SL₂(𝔽₄) acting on its four-dimensional projective representation V over 𝔽₂ is nearly adequate (BCGP25 Lemma 8.2.2, p. 182) and not adequate in the sense of Tho17 Definition 2.20, since H¹(A₅, ad/k) ≅ H²(A₅, k) ≅ k from the Schur multiplier ℤ/2 (BCGP25 Remark 8.2.3, p. 182).

nodes.title: The unavoidable dyadic dual Selmer class
nodes.statement: Keep the data of 1.1 with p = 2 and let T = S ∖ S_∞. Let K⁺_m be the maximal totally real subfield of ℚ(ζ_{2^m}), choose the least m with K⁺_m ⊄ F⁺ (so K⁺_{m−1} ⊂ F⁺), let L⁺ = F⁺K⁺_m, a totally real quadratic extension of F⁺ unramified outside 2, and let ψ ∈ H¹(F(S)/F⁺, ad r̄(1)) be the inflation of the nonzero class of H¹(L⁺/F⁺, k) through the scalars k ⊂ ad r̄. Prove that ψ ∈ H¹_{𝒮_Q^⊥,T} for every Taylor–Wiles datum (Q, (α_v)_{v∈Q}) of level N ≥ m (each v ∈ Q outside S, split completely in F(ζ_{2^N}), with ρ̄(Frob_v) semisimple with eigenvalue α_v); in particular h¹_{𝒮_Q^⊥,T} ≥ 1 for all such data and h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} ≥ 1 (BCGP25 Lemma 5.5.3 and proof, pp. 125–126).
prerequisites: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.3 (*Taylor–Wiles data with a residual eigenspace*)
proofSteps: ψ is trivial at infinite places because L⁺ is totally real, and at v ∈ Q because v splits completely in F(ζ_{2^N}) ⊃ L⁺. nodes.title: The universal ordinary Hecke algebra at p = 2
nodes.statement: Let G/F⁺ be the definite unitary group of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2 (*The definite unitary group attached to a CM field*), with ι_ṽ : G(O_{F⁺_v}) ≅ GL_n(O_{F_ṽ}) at split v, chosen places ṽ | v for v | 2, and Ĩ_2 the embeddings F → E inducing them. For λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Ĩ_2} let M_λ be the tensor product over τ ∈ Ĩ_2 of the O-lattices of highest weight λ_τ; for a set R ⊂ T ∖ S_2 of split places and characters χ_v : Iw(ṽ)/Iw_1(ṽ) ≅ (k(ṽ)^×)^n → O^× put M_{λ,{χ_v}} = M_λ ⊗ ⊗_{v∈R} O(χ_v). prerequisites: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2 (*The definite unitary group attached to a CM field*)

For n = 2 the Hecke polynomial at split w ∉ T is X² − T^1_w X + q_w T^2_w.

If n = 2 and F⁺ has two places above 2 with F⁺_v = ℚ₂ (d = 2, so nd = 4), then T(l) ≅ ({±1} × ℤ₂)^4, Spec Λ has 16 irreducible components, one for each character of {±1}^4, each of dimension 5 = dim Λ, and Λ[1/2] is regular.

The normalization is needed exactly when the scalar (w₀λ)(α^j_{ϖ_ṽ}) = ∏_τ τ(ϖ_ṽ)^{λ_{τ,n−j+1}+⋯+λ_{τ,n}} is not a unit. nodes.title: Hida theory at p = 2
nodes.statement:
Keep 2.1 with U(l^{b₀,b₀}) sufficiently small for some b₀ ≥ 1 and U_v hyperspecial at split v ∉ T. Prove (BCGP25 §5.7, pp. 132–133; Ger19 Proposition 2.5.3, Corollary 2.5.4, Lemma 2.4.4, Proposition 2.6.1, Lemma 2.6.4 and the proof of Corollary 3.1.4): 1. The Pontryagin dual of S^{ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), E/O) is finite free over O⟦T(l^{b₀})⟧; T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O) is a finite Λ-algebra and a finite faithful O⟦T(l^{b₀})⟧-algebra (Ger19 Corollary 2.5.4), and it and all finite-level ordinary Hecke algebras are reduced.
2. For a dominant λ, r ≥ 1 and c ≥ r, composing with the projection of M_λ onto its lowest weight line gives a Hecke-equivariant isomorphism S^{ord}_{λ,{χ_v}}(U(l^{c,c}), ϖ^{−r}O/O) ≅ S^{ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^{c,c}), ϖ^{−r}O/O) carrying U^j_λ to U^j_0 and twisting ⟨u⟩ by (w₀λ)(u).
3. The primes ℘_λ ⊂ Λ attached to dominant weights λ are Zariski dense in Spec Λ.
4. Hom_O(T^{T,ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O)/℘_λ, ℚ̄₂) = Hom_O(T^{T,ord}_{λ,{χ_v}}(U(l^{1,1}), O), ℚ̄₂) naturally (BCGP25 (5.7.4)). The route is Geraghty's, at l = 2: exactness of A ↦ S(U, A) and freeness over group rings follow from sufficient smallness (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups §7.5), the projection to the lowest weight line is B_n(O)-equivariant, and no step of Ger19 §§2.2–2.6 uses the parity of l.
acceptance: For n = 1, U^1_{λ,ϖ} acts on every algebraic character by a unit, so every character is ordinary and T^{T,ord} is the full Hecke algebra.
For λ = 0 the isomorphism of (2) is the identity and the twist (w₀λ)(u) of ⟨u⟩ is 1; for n = 2 and λ_τ = (1, 0) at one τ it twists ⟨u⟩ by τ(u_2), the lowest weight of M_λ.

Every O-algebra map T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞), O) → ℚ̄₂ above some ℘_λ comes from a classical ordinary form of weight λ and level U(l^{1,1}), by (4); a map above a prime of Λ that is not of the form ℘_λ need not.
T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O) is semilocal and finite over Λ, hence the product of its localizations at its finitely many maximal ideals.

Faithfulness over Λ fails. The scalar −1_n lies in T(l), since −1 ≡ 1 modulo every place above 2. If U_v ∋ −1_n at every finite v ∤ 2 (for instance U_v hyperspecial off R and U_v = ι_ṽ^{−1}Iw(ṽ) on R), then −1_n is a global central element and f(g·(−1_n)_2) = f(g·(−1_n)^{(2)}), so [−1_n] ∈ Λ acts on S^{ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), E/O) by the sign ε₀ = (−1)^{dn(n−1)/2}∏_{v∈R}∏_j χ_{v,j}(−1) = ∏_{v∈R}∏_j χ_{v,j}(−1) (nd ≡ 0 mod 4 makes the twist contribute 1). The nonzero element [−1_n] − ε₀ of Λ then acts by zero, so Λ → T^{T,ord} is not injective, although it is finite.

nodes.title: Ordinary constituents and ordinary RACSDC representations
nodes.statement: Keep 2.1 and fix ı : ℚ̄₂ ≅ ℂ. For λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Ĩ_2}, A_λ = colim_U S_λ(U, ℚ̄₂) is a semisimple admissible ℚ̄₂[G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺})]-module. Prove that the irreducible submodules of ıA_λ are the finite parts of descents to G of automorphic representations π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ, isobaric sums of conjugate self-dual representations, that after localization at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal only RACSDC π contribute, and that an irreducible submodule meets S^{ord}_λ(U(l^{b,b}), ℚ̄₂) for some b exactly when π is ι-ordinary, that is (ı^{−1}(⊗_{v|2} π_v))^{ord} ≠ 0 (BCGP25 §5.7, the paragraph defining A_λ, pp. 132–133). Prove moreover that every irreducible G(𝔸^{∞,R}_{F⁺}) × ∏_{v∈R} Iw(ṽ)-constituent π of S_{λ,{χ_v}}(ℚ̄₂) = colim_U S_{λ,{χ_v}}(U, ℚ̄₂) has a continuous semisimple r_2(π) : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄₂), unique up to isomorphism, such that: (i) for every finite place v ∉ S_2 ∪ R of F⁺ split as ww^c in F, (r_2(π)|G_{F_w})^{ss} ≅ (r_2(π_v ∘ ι_w^{−1})^∨(1 − n))^{ss}, so that at w with π_v unramified r_2(π)(Frob_w) has the Hecke polynomial of 2.1 as characteristic polynomial; (ii) r_2(π)^c ≅ r_2(π)^∨ε^{1−n}; (iii) r_2(π) is unramified above every inert v at which π_v has a vector fixed by a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup; (iv) for v ∈ R with π^{Iw(ṽ)} ≠ 0 and σ ∈ I_{F_ṽ}, r_2(π)(σ) has characteristic polynomial ∏_j (X − χ_{v,j}^{−1}(Art^{−1}_{F_ṽ}σ)) (Ger19 Proposition 2.7.2, stated for an arbitrary prime l, here at l = 2). This is the l = 2 case that PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2 (*Galois representations attached to constituents of algebraic modular forms*) does not state, its hypotheses requiring l odd.
prerequisites: PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0, PL.2 (*Base change and descent between definite unitary groups and GL_n*)
proofSteps: semisimplicity and admissibility come from the automorphic realization of AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups §7.5 (G(F⁺ ⊗ ℝ) is compact); base change and descent between G and GL_n are PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.2 (*Base change and descent between definite unitary groups and GL_n*, parts (1) and the first assertion of (2), which carry no condition on l); at a non-Eisenstein ideal the Galois representation is irreducible, forcing a cuspidal base change; ordinarity at Iwahori level is the principal-series criterion of PL.0 (*Principal-series characterisation of ι-ordinarity*) and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure §3.44. For r_2(π): the base change of π is an isobaric sum π₁ ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ π_s of discrete conjugate self-dual representations; each π_i is a Speh representation on a cuspidal conjugate self-dual σ_i, a twist of which by a power of |det| and an algebraic character is regular algebraic and essentially conjugate self-dual because π is cohomological (the infinitesimal character λ + ρ of ξ_λ is regular); r_2(π) is the corresponding sum of Tate twists of the 2-adic Galois representations of these twists (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.3, *Arbitrary regular conjugate-self-dual existence*, at ℓ = 2, with AG2.2, *Twisting an essentially self-dual form into unitary type*), as in Ger19's proof through Labesse Corollaire 5.3 and Chenevier–Harris Theorem 3.2.5. (i) at ramified split places is AG2.5 (*Caraiani's full away-prime compatibility*, every prime ℓ) up to semisimplification, which also gives (iv) through the characters χ_v; (ii) and (iii) follow from conjugate self-duality and unramified base change; uniqueness is Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt.
acceptance: For n = 1 the constituents are algebraic Hecke characters of weight λ and all are ordinary.

A maximal ideal of T^{T,ord}_λ is non-Eisenstein exactly when the attached residual representation is absolutely irreducible; for λ = 0 the constant functions span a constituent whose residual representation is a sum of characters, so its maximal ideal is Eisenstein and it is not RACSDC.
A RACSDC π whose local components above 2 are not ι-ordinary contributes to A_λ but meets no S^{ord}_λ(U(l^{b,b}), ℚ̄₂).

For n = 1, r_2(π) is the 2-adic character of the algebraic Hecke character x ↦ π(x/x^c) of 𝔸_F^×, and (ii) reads r^c = r^{−1}, since ε^{1−n} = 1; for λ = 0 and n ≥ 2 the constituent spanned by the constant functions has the non-cuspidal base change Speh(1, n) up to twist, and r_2(π) is a sum of n characters, consistent with its maximal ideal being Eisenstein (second Check). PL.2 states neither case at l = 2.

nodes.title: The ordinary global problem S_χ and R^{T,ord}
nodes.statement: Assume Hypothesis 5.7.1 and let π be an ordinary RACSDC automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) with ρ̄ = r̄_{π,2} : G_F → GL_n(k) absolutely irreducible. By Tho17 Lemma 2.2 (BCGP25 Lemma 5.1.2, p. 115) ρ̄ extends to r̄ : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(k) with ν ∘ r̄ = ε̄^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺} and r̄^{−1}(𝒢_n^0(k)) = G_F, unique up to 𝒢_n^0(k)-conjugacy. Let T ⊃ S_2 be a finite set of finite places of F⁺ split in F, R ⊂ T ∖ S_2, and χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n}) characters of O^×_{F_ṽ} trivial modulo ϖ for v ∈ R; assume Hypothesis 5.7.5: T contains the places under the ramification of π, and for v ∈ R, ρ̄|G_{F_ṽ} is trivial and π_ṽ^{Iw(ṽ)} ≠ 0. Put S = T ∪ S_∞, Λ_v = O for v ∉ S_2 and Λ_v = Λ_{GL_n,v} = O⟦I^{ab}_{F_ṽ}(2)^n⟧ for v ∈ S_2. Define the global problem (BCGP25 §5.7, Hypothesis 5.7.5, (5.7.6) and Definition 5.7.11, pp. 133–134) S_χ = (F, r̄, O, ε^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺}, S, {Λ_v}, {D^{χ_v}_v}_{v∈R} ∪ {D^△_v}_{v∈S_2} ∪ {Lift^□_v}_{v∈S∖(R∪S_2)}), where D^{χ_v}_v is the problem of lifts with inertial characteristic polynomial ∏_j (X − χ_{v,j}(Art^{−1}σ)^{−1}) (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §2.29) and D^△_v is Geraghty's ordinary problem (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §1.9 over §1.3). Local class field theory gives ⊗̂_{v∈S_2} Λ_v ≅ Λ, so R_{S_χ} and R^loc_{S_χ,T} are Λ-algebras. For R = ∅ write S^{T,ord} = S_χ and R^{T,ord} = R_{S_χ}.

nodes.title: The dimension bound
nodes.statement: In the setting of 3.1 (so S = T ⊔ S_∞, S_2 ⊂ T and every place of T splits in F), prove: (a) (The obstruction count.) Every irreducible component of Spec R_{S_χ} has dimension at least dim Λ − 1 = nd. (b) (BCGP25 Lemma 5.7.7 and proof, pp. 133–134, with the printed 1 + [F:ℚ]n corrected.) Every irreducible component of Spec R_{S_χ} has dimension at least dim Λ = 1 + nd.

Write R^T_{S_χ} = P/J with P = R^loc_{S_χ,T}⟦x_1, …, x_r⟧, r = h¹_{S_χ,T} (1.2(2)), and m_P the maximal ideal of P. The obstruction to lifting the universal T-framed lift from P/J to P/m_P J, relative to the local lifts given by R^loc_{S_χ,T} → P, is a class o ∈ H²_{S_χ,T} ⊗_k J/m_P J whose adjoint (J/m_P J)^∨ → H²_{S_χ,T} is injective (CHT08 Lemma 2.2.11 and Corollary 2.2.12, run with Thorne's complex C^•_{S_χ,T}), so J is generated by h²_{S_χ,T} elements. Krull's principal ideal theorem in each component of P, a complete local domain, gives every component of Spec R^T_{S_χ} dimension at least dim R^loc + h¹ − h². By 1.2(2)–(3) with q = 0, h¹ − h² = h⁰ − h³ − χ = −1 − (1 − #T + dn(n−1)/2); the −1 is h³_{S_χ,T} = 1, the term −h⁰(ad r̄(1)) of CHT08 Corollary 2.3.5. Hence every component of Spec R^T_{S_χ} has dimension at least (n² + 1)#T − 1 + nd, and subtracting the (n² + 1)#T − 1 framing variables (1.1) gives nd.

(b) the count of (a) is one relation short, and (b) follows once J is generated by h²_{S_χ,T} − 1 elements, that is once the image of (J/m_P J)^∨ lies in a hyperplane of H²_{S_χ,T} ≅ (H¹_{S_χ^⊥,T})^∨ (1.2(2)). The hyperplane is that of the unavoidable class ψ of 1.4, which lies in H¹_{S_χ^⊥,T} because the argument of 1.4 does not depend on the local problems at T: the step to prove is ⟨o, ψ⟩ = 0 in J/m_P J. A route: det : 𝒢_n → 𝒢_1, (g, a) ↦ (det g, a^n), j ↦ j, is a homomorphism (both sides of j(g, a)j^{−1} = (a·ᵗg^{−1}, a) map to (a^n·det g^{−1}, a^n)), and its derivative on ad r̄ = M_n(k) is the trace, adjoint under the trace pairing to the scalar inclusion k(1) → ad r̄(1) through which ψ is defined. Functoriality of Thorne's complexes and of their duality gives ⟨o, ψ⟩ = ⟨tr_* o, ψ′⟩, where ψ′ is the class of L⁺/F⁺ in the rank-one dual Selmer group and tr_* o is the image of the universal obstruction o_1 of the rank-one problem of det ∘ r (multiplier χ^n δ^{n+1}_{F/F⁺}, all lifts at T) under the map of rank-one presentations into P/J. So it suffices that ⟨o_1, ψ′⟩ = 0. In rank one both rings are completed group rings, by class field theory: the global ring is O⟦Γ⟧ with framing variables, Γ the largest pro-2 quotient of G^{ab}_{F,S} on which c acts by inversion (ℤ₂-rank d), and the local ring is ⊗̂_{v∈T} O⟦F_ṽ^×(2)⟧, F_ṽ^×(2) the pro-2 completion of F_ṽ^×, mapping to it through the local Artin maps; ⟨o_1, ψ′⟩ = 0 is a computation with this map and the Kummer class of L⁺/F⁺. The source states (b) without this step (source issue below); the reduction to rank one and the rank-one computation are part of this target.
acceptance: The bound of (b) is 1 + nd, not the printed 1 + n[F:ℚ] = 1 + 2nd: for n = 2, d = 2, #T = 3 the local ring has dimension 1 + 12 + 6 = 19, (b) gives 19 − 14 = 5 = dim Λ for R_{S_χ}, and the printed value 9 would contradict finiteness of R^{T,ord} over the five-dimensional Λ (4.7).

The same numbers in (a): h¹ − h² = −1 − (1 − 3 + 2) = −1, so every component of Spec R^T_{S_χ} has dimension at least 18 and of Spec R_{S_χ} at least 4 = dim Λ − 1; the printed count, which uses h³ = 0, gets 5 only by omitting the −1.

Rank one, where everything is explicit: with n = 1 the count of (a) gives dim R^loc_1 + h¹ − h² − (2#T − 1) = (1 + #T + d) + (#T − 2) − (2#T − 1) = d, while class field theory gives dim O⟦Γ⟧ = 1 + d (the ℤ₂-rank of the part of G^{ab}_{F,S}(2) on which c acts by −1 is d, the Leopoldt defects of F and F⁺ being equal). Prove that there are a maximal ideal m of T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O) and a surjection of Λ-algebras R_{S_χ} → T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O)_m, and that the corresponding r_m : G_{F⁺} → 𝒢_n(T^{T,ord}_{{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), O)_m), unique up to strict equivalence, is characterized by: for every finite place v ∉ T split as ww^c in F, r_m is unramified at w and w^c and r_m(Frob_w) has characteristic polynomial X^n + ⋯ + (−1)^j q_w^{j(j−1)/2}T^j_w X^{n−j} + ⋯ + (−1)^n q_w^{n(n−1)/2}T^n_w (BCGP25 Proposition 5.7.9 and proof, p. 134).

nodes.title: Uniform local fixed vectors
nodes.statement: Let w ∤ 2 be a finite place of the CM field F and π a RACSDC automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F). Prove that there is a compact open subgroup U_w ⊂ GL_n(O_{F_w}), depending only on r̄_{π,2}|G_{F_w}, such that every RACSDC π′ with r̄_{π′,2} ≅ r̄_{π,2} has (π′_w)^{U_w} ≠ 0 (BCGP25 Lemma 5.7.12 and proof, p. 134).
proofSteps: Spec R^□[1/2] of r̄_{π,2}|G_{F_w} has finitely many components, on each of which the restriction to inertia of the Weil–Deligne representation is constant (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §2.24). By gap:inertial-types-and-block-levels (i) they meet finitely many Bernstein blocks, and by (ii) each block has a compact open U with fixed vectors in every irreducible member; U_w is the intersection.

The conductor of the seed π alone does not bound the others: for n = 1 and q_w ≡ 1 mod 4, characters of k(w)^× of order 4 are ≡ 1 modulo the maximal ideal and give lifts of conductor 1 of the trivial residual character, while the seed may be unramified.

nodes.title: Solvable preparation and the auxiliary place
nodes.statement: Assume (1)–(6). Prove that there is a solvable CM extension F′/F, linearly disjoint over F from the field cut out by ρ̄, such that, with T′ the places of F′⁺ above T and E enlarged: (1)–(6) hold over F′ with ρ̄(G_{F′}) = ρ̄(G_F); F′ = F′⁺(√−1); ρ̄|G_{F′_ṽ} is trivial for v ∈ T′; [F′⁺_v:ℚ₂] > n(n−1)/2 + 1 for v | 2; and for v ∈ T′ ∖ S_2, π_{F′,ṽ}^{Iw(ṽ)} ≠ 0, q_v ≡ 1 mod 2^N with 2^N > n and O containing a primitive 2^N-th root of unity, where 2^N ∥ q_v − 1, and every lift of ρ̄|G_{F_u} (u the place of F under ṽ, v ∈ T ∖ S_2, the original field) becomes unipotently ramified on restriction to G_{F′_w} for every place w of F′ above u (BCGP25 Lemma 5.6.2, p. 128). nodes.title: Patched modules for the unipotent and distinct-character problems
nodes.statement: In the situation of 4.1 (over F′, written F), write T = S_2 ⊔ {v₁} ⊔ R, choose for v ∈ R pairwise distinct characters χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n} of O^×_{F_ṽ} trivial modulo ϖ, and let S_1, S_χ be the problems of 3.1. Take U_v = G(O_{F⁺_v}) at split v ∉ T, hyperspecial at inert v, U_v = Iw(ṽ) for v ∈ R and U_{v₁} torsion-free. Let m₁ ⊂ T^{T,ord}_{{1}}(U(l^∞), O) be the maximal ideal of ρ̄ and m_χ the corresponding ideal (S^{ord}_{0,{χ_v}}(U(l^∞), k) = S^{ord}_{0,{1}}(U(l^∞), k)), and H_χ, H_1 the Pontryagin duals of the localized ordinary forms, so H_χ/ϖ ≅ H_1/ϖ. Put q = h¹_{𝒮^⊥,T} − 1, g = q + #T − 1 − dn(n−1)/2, S_∞ = Λ⟦X_1, …, X_{q+(n²+1)#T−1}⟧, R_{1,∞} = R^loc_{S_1,T}⟦Y_1, …, Y_g⟧ and R_{χ,∞} = R^loc_{S_χ,T}⟦Y_1, …, Y_g⟧. Prove that the patching data of 4.2 exist for both problems with compatible identifications modulo ϖ, and that dim R_{1,∞} = dim R_{χ,∞} = nd + (n²+1)#T + q = dim S_∞, so that each H_{·,∞} has maximal depth over R_{·,∞} and support a union of irreducible components (BCGP25 proof of Theorem 5.7.14, pp. 136–137, with (5.7.16)–(5.7.17)).
proofSteps: Taylor–Wiles data of every level with #Q_N = q and g variables come from 1.2(4), whose hypotheses (i)–(iv) hold after 4.1; one dual Selmer class always survives (1.4), whence q = h¹ − 1. The Hecke modules at level Q_N are finite free over Λ[Δ_{Q_N}] by sufficient smallness and 2.2(1), and the Galois representations at level Q_N come from 3.3. Patch with 4.2. Dimensions: every component of R^loc has dimension 1 + n²#T + dn(n+1)/2 here, since ρ̄ is trivial at T and the local degrees above 2 are large (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §§6.24, 2.29, 2.24), so dim R_{·,∞} = 1 + n²#T + dn(n+1)/2 + g = nd + (n²+1)#T + q = dim Λ + q + (n²+1)#T − 1.

nodes.title: Components of the patched rings
nodes.statement: In the situation of 4.3, prove for each minimal prime Q of Λ (BCGP25 proof of Theorem 5.7.14, list (1)–(5), p. 137; BCGNT25 Lemma 3.2.4 and proof, pp. 33–34): (1) the generic points of R_{χ,∞}/Q and R_{1,∞}/Q have characteristic 0; (2) the irreducible components of Spec R_{χ,∞}/Q and of Spec R_{1,∞}/Q biject with products over v ∈ R ∪ {v₁} of irreducible components C_v of the local rings; (3) the irreducible components of Spec R_{χ,∞}/(Q, ϖ) = Spec R_{1,∞}/(Q, ϖ) biject with products of irreducible components C̄_v of the special fibres of the local rings; (4) the irreducible components of Spec R_{χ,∞}/Q biject with those of Spec R^□_{v₁}; (5) for each component C̄ = ⊗C̄_v of Spec R_{1,∞}/(Q, ϖ) there are components C_v of Spec R^1_v (v ∈ R) and components C^1_{v₁}, …, C^s_{v₁} of Spec R^□_{v₁} (s ≥ 1) such that the components of Spec R_{1,∞}/Q generalizing C̄ are exactly the C^i_{v₁} ⊗ ⊗_{v∈R} C_v.
proofSteps: components of a completed tensor product of local rings whose components are geometrically irreducible of characteristic 0 are products of local components, in the generic and the special fibre (BLGHT11 Lemma 3.3 as used in BCGNT25 Lemma 3.2.4; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §4.6), and power series variables do not change this. Above 2, R^△_v/Q is geometrically irreducible with generically reduced special fibre (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §6.24). At v ∈ R, R^{χ_v}_v is irreducible with characteristic-0 generic point and every prime of R^1_v minimal over ϖ contains a unique minimal prime (§2.29), R^1_v/ϖ = R^{χ_v}_v/ϖ. At v₁ the lifting ring has finitely many components, all of characteristic 0 (§2.24); unique generalizations come from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §6.7.
acceptance: Each generic point of the special fibre of R_{1,∞}/Q generalizes to components that differ only in their v₁-factor.
If #R = 0, (2) and (4) say that the components of Spec R_{1,∞}/Q are those of Spec R^□_{v₁}.
For n = 2 and v ∈ R, R^{χ_v}_v with χ_{v,1} ≠ χ_{v,2} is irreducible, while R^1_v has two components (unramified and Steinberg-type), so (2) for S_1 has twice as many components per v as for S_χ.

nodes.title: Component support by Ihara avoidance
nodes.statement: In the situation of 4.3, prove (BCGP25 proof of Theorem 5.7.14, from "Fix for the moment a minimal prime Q" to the existence of π_Y, pp. 137–138): (a) for every minimal prime Q of Λ and every set X of irreducible components C_v of Spec R^1_v (v ∈ R) there is an irreducible component C_{X,v₁} of Spec R^□_{v₁} such that the component C_X = C_{X,v₁} ⊗ ⊗_{v∈R} C_v of Spec R_{1,∞}/Q (4.4(2)) lies in the support of H_{1,∞}; with R^loc_X the quotient of R^loc_{S_1,T}/Q by the prime of C_{X,v₁} ⊗ ⊗_{v∈R} C_v and R_X = R_{S_1} ⊗_{R^loc_{S_1,T}} R^loc_X, Spec R_X lies in the support of H_1, (R_X)_red is a quotient of T^{T,ord}_{{1}}(U(l^∞), O)_{m₁}, R_X is a finite Λ-algebra and every component of Spec R_X has dimension at least dim Λ; (b) for every choice Y of irreducible components C_v of the local rings at v ∈ R ∪ S_2 there is an ordinary RACSDC π_Y with r̄_{π_Y,2} ≅ ρ̄, r_{π_Y,2} unramified outside T, and r_{π_Y,2}|G_{F_ṽ} lying on C_v and on no other component for each v ∈ R ∪ S_2.
proofSteps: the seed π gives a nonempty support of H_{1,∞}; by the identification modulo ϖ the support of H_{χ,∞} is nonempty, and by 4.4(4) it is a union of components of R_{χ,∞}/Q, each indexed by a component of R^□_{v₁}; by 4.4(5) and the identification modulo ϖ (Taylor's Ihara avoidance) a product C_{X,v₁} ⊗ ⊗C_v lies in the support of H_{1,∞}. Then Spec R_X ⊂ Supp H_1, so (R_X)_red is a Hecke quotient, finite over Λ by 2.2(1); R_X is finite by DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §4.1. The dimension bound for R_X is read off the patched module, so no appeal to 3.2 is needed here. Inside Spec R_{1,∞}, the closed set V(I_X) cut out by the kernel I_X of R^loc_{S_1,T} → R^loc_X is the single component C_X, because R^△_v/Q is irreducible above 2 (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §6.24) and components are products of local components (4.4(2)). Since R_{1,∞}/a_∞ ↠ R_{S_1}, H_1 = H_{1,∞}/a_∞ and Supp(H_{1,∞}/a_∞) = Supp H_{1,∞} ∩ V(a_∞), we get Spec R_X = Spec R_{S_1} ∩ V(I_X) = Supp H_{1,∞} ∩ V(a_∞) ∩ C_X = C_X ∩ V(a_∞), using C_X ⊂ Supp H_{1,∞}. C_X is a complete local domain of dimension dim S_∞ (4.3), so by Krull's height theorem every irreducible component of C_X ∩ V(a_∞), that is of Spec R_X, has dimension at least dim S_∞ − (q + (n²+1)#T − 1) = dim Λ, and being finite over the domain Λ/Q of the same dimension it maps onto Spec Λ/Q. Choose λ with R_X/℘_λ nonzero, finite over O and of dimension ≥ 1; it has a ℚ̄₂-point (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §4.2), which by 2.2(4) and 2.3 comes from an ordinary RACSDC π_Y. Repeating over the minimal primes Q runs through the components above 2, and genericity of π_{Y,ṽ} puts its local representations on a single component (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.1).
acceptance: Every choice of local components at R ∪ S_2 is realized by an automorphic lift of ρ̄.
The support statement is for H_1, the module over F; the module over the second base change belongs to 4.6 (source issue: the printed text writes H′_{1,∞} here).

nodes.statement: Assume (1)–(6) and let R^{T,ord} be the ring of 3.1 (R = ∅). Prove that R^{T,ord} is a finite Λ-algebra (BCGP25 Theorem 5.7.14, first assertion, and the end of its proof, pp. 134–135 and 139). This is a headline of the roadmap.

nodes.title: The dyadic ordinary reduced R = T theorem
nodes.statement: Assume (1)–(6), let R^{T,ord} be as in 4.7 and T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m the localized universal ordinary Hecke algebra (2.1) with the surjection of 3.3. If U_v is sufficiently deep (3.5) for every v ∈ T ∖ S_2, prove that R^{T,ord} → T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m has nilpotent kernel, so (R^{T,ord})_red ≅ T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m (BCGP25 Theorem 5.7.14, second assertion, and the last paragraph of its proof, pp. 135 and 139). This is the headline of Layers 1–4.
proofSteps: by 4.7 and 3.2(b) every component of Spec R^{T,ord} dominates a component of Spec Λ, so the ℚ̄₂-points above the ℘_λ (dense by 2.2(3)) are dense in Spec R^{T,ord}. Each such point is automorphic: its restriction to G_L is a point of R′_{L/F,T′}, hence of the Hecke algebra over L (4.6), hence of an ordinary RACSDC representation over L by 2.2(4), and it is automorphic over F by soluble descent (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.0, *Soluble base change and descent of automorphy*). Sufficient depth puts it at level U(l^{1,1}), so it lies in Spec T^{T,ord}(U(l^∞))_m. A closed subset containing a dense set is everything, so the kernel lies in every prime (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §6.5).
acceptance: Without the depth hypothesis the theorem still gives finiteness (4.7), but automorphic points may need a smaller level than U, so the kernel need not be nilpotent.

The density step uses 3.2(b), whose scalar-direction step is part of that target and is not in the sources; the obstruction count 3.2(a) alone leaves room for a component of dimension dim Λ − 1, finite over Λ, lying over a divisor of Spec Λ that contains no ℘_λ.
For n = 2 and the 16-component Λ of the Examples of Layer 2 the conclusion holds component by component of Λ.

nodes.title: GSp₄-reasonable residual representations
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, k a finite field of characteristic p, F a number field and ρ̄ : G_F → GSp₄(k) continuous and absolutely GSp₄-irreducible (its image lies in no proper parabolic subgroup over k̄). Let 𝔰𝔭₄ be the Lie algebra of Sp₄ over k (Mathlib `LieAlgebra.Symplectic.sp`) with the adjoint action of GSp₄(k), 𝔰𝔭₄^∨ its dual, and for semisimple h ∈ GSp₄(k) let 𝔷_h = Lie Z(Z_{GSp₄}(h)) ∩ 𝔰𝔭₄. Define a subgroup H ⊂ GSp₄(k) to satisfy the reasonableness conditions if (a) H⁰(H, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0 and (b) for every nonzero simple k[H]-submodule W ⊂ 𝔰𝔭₄^∨ there are a semisimple h ∈ H, w ∈ W and z ∈ 𝔷_h with w(z) ≠ 0; and ρ̄ to be GSp₄-reasonable if for all sufficiently large n the group H_n = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^n})}) satisfies (a) and (b) and, when ζ_p lies in the field cut out by 𝔰𝔭₄^∨, also H¹(H_n, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0 (WHI22 Definitions 3.15 and 3.19 and Lemma 3.20, pp. 21–24; WHI22 v4 renames the notion).
acceptance: If ρ̄ has image in the diagonal torus, H⁰(H_n, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) contains the dual of the Cartan subalgebra, so (a) fails and ρ̄ is not GSp₄-reasonable.

If ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_3)}) ⊇ Sp₄(𝔽₃), then, Sp₄(𝔽₃) being perfect and enormous (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §7.11), every H_n contains Sp₄(𝔽₃) and ρ̄ is vast, hence GSp₄-reasonable; yet Sp₄(𝔽₃) ⊂ GL₄(𝔽₃) is not adequate as a subgroup of GL₄, because H¹(Sp₄(𝔽₃), ∧²) ≠ 0 (BCGP25 Remark 6.4.5, p. 151), so reasonableness is a symplectic condition.
For regular semisimple h in the diagonal torus of GSp₄ with p > 2, the trace form on 𝔷_h = 𝔱 is 2(xx′ + yy′), nondegenerate; for p = 2 it vanishes, which is why p ≥ 3 is assumed.

nodes.title: Taylor–Wiles places for GSp₄-reasonable residual representations
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 3, 𝒮 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_v}, {D_v}) a GSp₄ problem (5.1) over a totally real F⁺, T ⊂ S with S_p ⊂ T, and n ≥ 1. Let L be the field cut out by 𝔰𝔭₄^∨ and suppose that H = ρ̄(G_{F⁺(ζ_{p^n})}) satisfies (a) and (b) of 5.2 and that either ζ_p ∉ L or H¹(H, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0. Let q ≥ h¹(G_{F⁺,S}, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)). Prove that there is a set Q of Taylor–Wiles places of level n (v ∉ S, q_v ≡ 1 mod p^n, ρ̄ unramified at v with ρ̄(Frob_v) semisimple, with the local problem of gap:gsp4-semisimple-taylor-wiles-places) with #Q = q and H¹_{𝒮_Q^⊥,T}(𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)) = 0 (WHI22 Proposition 3.18 and proof, pp. 22–23, with the hypothesis (a) that its proof uses).
proofSteps: (i) WHI22 Lemma 3.16: if H⁰(H, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0 and either ζ_p ∉ L or H¹(H, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0, then H¹(Gal(L(ζ_{p^n})/F⁺), 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)) = 0 (the proof is that of BCGP21 Lemma 7.5.9); this step is part of this target, since ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §7.11 states it only under ζ_p ∉ L or enormous image. (ii) By WHI22 Lemma 3.14 and the dual condition L_v^⊥ = H¹_ur(F_v, M_v^∨(1)) of the gap, a class [ψ] is killed by adding v exactly when its image in H¹_ur(F_v, N_v^∨(1)) is nonzero, N_v = Lie Z(M_{ρ̄(Frob_v)}) ∩ 𝔰𝔭₄; this quotient detects classes and is not L_v^⊥. (iii) By (i), ψ restricts to a nonzero G_{F⁺(ζ_{p^n})}-equivariant homomorphism f : G_{L(ζ_{p^n})} → 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1); condition (b) for a simple submodule of the span of its image gives semisimple σ₀, and σ = σ₀ or τσ₀ with ψ(σ)(z) ≠ 0. (iv) Chebotarev gives infinitely many v with ρ̄(Frob_v) = ρ̄(σ), ψ(Frob_v) = ψ(σ) and Frob_v ∈ G_{F⁺(ζ_{p^n})}; induct on the dimension.
acceptance: The Frobenius at a Taylor–Wiles place need only be semisimple; for ρ̄(Frob_v) = 1 one has M = GSp₄, N_v = 𝔰𝔭₄ ∩ Lie Z(GSp₄) = 0 and v detects no class, so such places are useless though allowed.

For a reasonable image H with ζ_p ∈ L that is not enormous, Lemma 3.16 applies through H¹(H, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) = 0, while the statement of ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §7.11 does not; this is why (i) is proved here.

Without (a), H⁰(H, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨) ≠ 0 (for instance a torus image) and the inflation–restriction kernel H¹(Gal(L(ζ_{p^n})/F⁺), 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)) need not vanish, so the restriction to G_{L(ζ_{p^n})} of a nonzero class can be zero.

nodes.title: Ordinary GSp₄ seed data
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 split completely in the totally real field F⁺ and fix ı : ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p. Define an ordinary GSp₄ seed datum as: an ordinary cuspidal automorphic representation π of GSp₄(𝔸_{F⁺}) of general type (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions §3.9) with central character |·|² and weights ((k_v, l_v; 2))_{v|∞}, k_v ≥ l_v ≥ 2, with its Galois representation ρ_{π,p} (gap:gsp4-galois-representations-totally-real) and residual representation ρ̄; a finite set R of finite places prime to p containing the prime-to-p places where π ramifies; an ordinary p-stabilization (α_v, β_v) of ρ̄|G_{F⁺_v} for each v | p; and a place w₀; such that (BCGP25 §6.3, Hypothesis 6.3.1, Remarks 6.3.2–6.3.3 and the choice of w₀, pp. 146–147): (1) ρ̄ is GSp₄-reasonable (5.2); (2) ρ̄ is tidy (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations §7.11); (3) for v | p, ρ̄|G_{F⁺_v} is ordinary of weight 2 with p-stabilization (α_v, β_v) compatible with a fixed ordinary p-stabilization of π_v; (4) for v | p, ρ_{π,p}|G_{F⁺_v}, viewed through the stabilization as a point of R^△_v (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §6.29), lies on a unique irreducible component of Spec R^△_v; (5) for v ∈ R, ρ̄|G_{F⁺_v} is trivial, q_v ≡ 1 mod p (mod 9 if p = 3) and π_v^{Iw(v)} ≠ 0; (6) w₀ is an unramified place of residue characteristic > 5 with q_{w₀} ≢ 1 mod p such that no two eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_{w₀}) have ratio q_{w₀}. Put S = S_p ∪ R ∪ {w₀}.
acceptance: If ρ̄|G_{F⁺_v} is residually p-distinguished, condition (4) holds automatically, since Spec R^△_v[1/p] is irreducible (BCGP25 Remark 6.3.2).
For p = 3 a place v ∈ R must have q_v ≡ 1 mod 9: q_v = 19 is allowed and q_v = 7 is not.
A place w₀ with q_{w₀} ≡ 1 mod p is excluded: every eigenvalue has ratio 1 = q_{w₀} with itself, so H⁰(G_{F⁺_{w₀}}, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) ⊇ 𝔱 ≠ 0.
If π is unramified at every prime-to-p place, R may be empty and S = S_p ∪ {w₀}.

nodes.title: The selected ordinary problems S_1 and S_{1,π}
nodes.statement: Let (π, (α_v, β_v), R, w₀) be an ordinary GSp₄ seed datum with S = S_p ∪ R ∪ {w₀}. For v | p let D^△_v be the ordinary problem of LocalGaloisDeformationRings §6.29 over Λ_{GSp₄,v} with unramified characters χ_1(Frob_v) = α_v and χ_2(Frob_v) = β_v; for v ∈ R let D^1_v be the unipotently ramified problem (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §2.22 with trivial characters); let D^□_{w₀} be all lifts. Define S_1 = (ρ̄, S, {Λ_{GSp₄,v}}_{v∈S_p} ∪ {O}_{v∈S∖S_p}, {D^△_v}_{v∈S_p} ∪ {D^1_v}_{v∈R} ∪ {D^□_{w₀}}) over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}; for v | p let R^{△,π}_v be the quotient of R^△_v by the minimal prime of the unique component through ρ_{π,p}|G_{F⁺_v} (seed condition (4)); and let S_{1,π} replace D^△_v by the problem of R^{△,π}_v (BCGP25 §6.3, from "By the above hypotheses" to the definition of T_{S_{1,π}}, p. 147).

If the seed point lay on two components, "the component through π" would not be defined; seed condition (4) excludes this.

nodes.title: The Galois representation over the GSp₄ Hida–Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: In the setting of 5.5, let M¹ be the finite free Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-module of gap:hilbert-siegel-hida-module-free and T_{S_1} the Hida–Hecke algebra acting faithfully on it. Prove that there is a continuous ρ : G_{F⁺} → GSp₄(T_{S_1}) of type S_1, unique up to strict equivalence, whose Frobenius characteristic polynomials at v ∉ S are the Hecke polynomials Q_v(X), giving a surjection R_{S_1} ↠ T_{S_1} of Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-algebras; the same holds for the Taylor–Wiles variants M^{1,Q}, compatibly with Δ_Q. Put T_{S_{1,π}} = R_{S_{1,π}} ⊗_{R_{S_1}} T_{S_1} (BCGP25 §6.3, p. 147; WHI22 Theorems 7.7–7.8 and proofs, pp. 64–65; BCGP21 Theorem 7.9.4).
proofSteps: embed T_{S_1} into a ring of tuples (a, (a_π)) ⊂ k × ∏_π O_{E_π} indexed by the classical ordinary π of large regular weight contributing to M¹ (gap:hilbert-siegel-ordinary-classicality), glue their Galois representations (gap:gsp4-galois-representations-totally-real) and pass to Artinian quotients. The flag-image condition D^△_v is a scheme-theoretic image, not understood on Artinian rings; but T_{S_1} is reduced, O-flat and embeds in ∏_π O_{E_π}, so R^□_v → T_{S_1} factors through R^△_v once every composite R^□_v → O_{E_π} does, that is once each ρ_π|G_{F⁺_v} is ordinary with stabilization lifting (α_v, β_v) (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §6.3); only the O_{E′}-points of D^△_v are used.
acceptance: T_{S_1} is finite over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}, acting faithfully on a finite free module.
The k-coordinate of a tuple (a, (a_π)) is determined by the others, so the factoring through R^△_v is tested on O_{E′}-points only.
For F⁺ = ℚ and ρ̄ residually p-distinguished, the construction is that of BCGP21 Theorem 7.9.4 with D^{B,α_p}.

Constructs the Galois representation over the Hida–Hecke algebra with Taylor–Wiles data by embedding the Hecke algebra in a product of rings of integers indexed by classical ordinary forms of large weight and gluing.

nodes.title: The automorphic ordinary component dominates the local weight space
nodes.statement: Prove that for every v | p the composite Spec R^{△,π}_v → Spec Λ_{GSp₄,v} is surjective; consequently some minimal prime of R^{△,π}_v/(p) contains the minimal prime of R^{△,π}_v and no other minimal prime of R^△_v, and R^{△,π}_v has relative dimension 16 over O (BCGP25 proof of Theorem 6.3.4, first paragraph, p. 148; Lemma 6.2.6, pp. 145–146).
proofSteps: let Q_π ⊂ T_{S_1} be a minimal prime contained in the prime of π; R^△_v → T_{S_1}/Q_π factors through R^{△,π}_v by seed condition (4). The composite Spec T_{S_1}/Q_π → Spec Λ_{GSp₄,v} is surjective because T_{S_1}/Q_π is finite and torsion-free over the domain Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}, so lying over applies. This is the hypothesis of LocalGaloisDeformationRings §6.35 (BCGP25 Lemma 6.2.6), whose conclusion is the second sentence.
acceptance: The hypothesis of Lemma 6.2.6 is checked globally, not by a local analysis of R^△_v.
For p > 2 split completely Λ_{GSp₄,v} = O⟦x, y⟧ is a domain; at p = 2 it would have torsion and the lying-over argument would need each component separately.
Relative dimension 16 over O above p is 14 over Λ_{GSp₄,v}, matching the count of 6.2.

nodes.title: Patched Hida modules for the selected problem
nodes.statement: Enlarge E to contain µ_p (µ_9 if p = 3) and fix, for v ∈ R, characters χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, χ_{v,2}) nontrivial and trivial mod λ with χ_{v,1} ≠ χ_{v,2}^{±1}; let S_χ be S_1 with D^{χ_v}_v (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §2.22) in place of D^1_v. Let q = h¹(G_{F⁺,S}, 𝔰𝔭₄^∨(1)) and, by WHI22 Lemma 7.10 built from 5.3, fix 0 ≤ t ≤ 2q and Taylor–Wiles data Q_N of level N with #Q_N = q and Δ_{Q_N} having t cyclic factors. Let Δ_∞ = ℤ_p^t ↠ Δ_{Q_N}, S_∞ = 𝒯⟦Δ_∞⟧ with 𝒯 the framing ring over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} (5.1) and augmentation ideal a_∞, R^1_∞ and R^χ_∞ power series rings in g = t − 4d + #S − 1 variables over R^loc_{S_1,S} and R^loc_{S_χ,S}, and R_{∞,π} = R^1_∞ ⊗_{R^loc_{S_1,S}} R^loc_{S_{1,π},S}. Prove that there are Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-algebra maps S_∞ → R^1_∞ → R_{S_1} and S_∞ → R^χ_∞ → R_{S_χ}, S_∞-modules M^1_∞ and M^χ_∞ finite free over S_∞ with M^·_∞/a_∞ ≅ M^· (5.6), compatible actions of R^·_∞, and identifications M^1_∞/λ ≅ M^χ_∞/λ compatible with R^1_∞/λ ≅ R^χ_∞/λ; and that M^·_∞ is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R^·_∞ with dim (R^·_∞)′ = dim S_∞, ′ denoting the maximal O-flat quotient (BCGP25 proof of Theorem 6.3.4, p. 148; WHI22 §7.3, Lemma 7.10 and Proposition 7.11 with proof, pp. 66–68).
proofSteps: the Taylor–Wiles data are those of WHI22 Lemma 7.10 (#Q_N = q, with t the number of cyclic factors of Δ_{Q_N}, which varies with N and is fixed by passing to a subsequence); the modules M^{·,Q_N} are finite free over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}[Δ_{Q_N}] with coinvariants M^· (gap:hilbert-siegel-taylor-wiles-coinvariants) and carry the Galois representations of 5.6. Since Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} is a power series ring, the patching is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra Layer 8 (§§8.2–8.5) with complexes concentrated in one degree and δ = 1. Dimensions: S_∞ is formally smooth over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} of relative dimension t + 11#S − 1, and (R^·_∞)′ is equidimensional of relative dimension g + 10#S + 4d over it (14 over Λ_{GSp₄,v} above p by LocalGaloisDeformationRings §6.31, 10 over O at R and at w₀ by §§2.22 and 1.22); with g = t − 4d + #S − 1 these agree, so a module free over S_∞ is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over (R^·_∞)′.
acceptance: For F⁺ = ℚ, #S = 3 and t = 7: g = 7 − 4 + 3 − 1 = 5, the relative dimension of (R_∞)′ is 5 + 30 + 4 = 39 and that of S_∞ is 7 + 33 − 1 = 39.

The number of places in Q_N is q, while t, the number of cyclic factors of Δ_{Q_N}, can be up to 2q because the Levi centres at semisimple Frobenius have rank up to 2; using t for #Q_N would miscount.
With I = ∅ the patched modules are free over S_∞; there is no defect, unlike the Klingen case #I = 1 of BCGP21 where they are only balanced.

nodes.title: The symplectic ordinary reduced R = T theorem
nodes.statement: Prove that the map R_{S_{1,π}} → T_{S_{1,π}} has nilpotent kernel, so (R_{S_{1,π}})_red ≅ T_{S_{1,π}}: R = T holds up to nilpotents on exactly the chosen local components above p (BCGP25 Theorem 6.3.4 and proof, pp. 148–149; Remark 6.3.2, p. 147). This is the headline of Layers 5–6.
proofSteps: it suffices that the support of M¹_∞ contains every irreducible component of Spec R_{∞,π}. (i) The seed: ρ_{π,p} with its stabilizations is a point of Supp_{R_{S_1}} M¹ lying on Spec R_{S_{1,π}}, so Supp M¹_∞ contains the component C_π of Spec R_{∞,π} through it. (ii) By 6.1 (LocalGaloisDeformationRings §6.35) the special fibre of C_π contains an irreducible component Z of Spec R_{∞,π}/λ lying on no other component of Spec R^1_∞, the factors at R (§2.22) and at w₀ (formal smoothness, §1.22) contributing single components. (iii) Ihara avoidance: Z ⊂ Supp M¹_∞/λ = Supp M^χ_∞/λ; a component of Supp M^χ_∞ generalizing Z has special fibre through Z, so its factor above p is R^{△,π}_v; the χ-side local rings at R are irreducible (§2.22), so R^χ_{∞,π} is irreducible after enlarging E and M^χ_∞ has full support on it (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §9.6). Reducing modulo λ, Supp M¹_∞/λ contains Spec R_{∞,π}/λ. (iv) Every component of Supp M¹_∞ and of Spec R_{∞,π} has dimension dim S_∞, so M¹_∞ is supported on a component of R_{∞,π} as soon as it is supported at a special-fibre point lying on that component alone; such points exist factor by factor (6.1 above p, §2.22 at R, §1.22 at w₀). (v) Hence Spec R_{S_{1,π}} ⊂ Supp M¹, and since T_{S_1} acts faithfully on M¹ the kernel is nilpotent (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §6.5).
acceptance: The theorem is "minimal at p": it identifies R and T only on the components selected by the seed; a component of Spec R^△_v not through the seed is not claimed.
Nonvanishing of M^χ_∞ alone does not suffice in (iii): it gives some component of Supp M^χ_∞, possibly with a factor above p other than R^{△,π}_v; the seed point and Z are what select R^{△,π}_v.
In the residually p-distinguished case the theorem is a special case of BCGP21 and WHI22 Theorem 7.12.

nodes.title: Finiteness of the selected symplectic ordinary deformation ring
nodes.statement: Prove that R_{S_{1,π}} is a finite Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-algebra (BCGP25 Theorem 6.3.4, p. 148). This is a headline of the roadmap.
proofSteps: T_{S_1}, and hence its quotient T_{S_{1,π}}, is finite over Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺} (5.6); by 6.3 the kernel of R_{S_{1,π}} → T_{S_{1,π}} is nilpotent, so R_{S_{1,π}}/m_Λ R_{S_{1,π}} has finite length and R_{S_{1,π}} is finite (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra §4.1).
acceptance: Finiteness is what BCGP25 Proposition 7.5.10 uses at p > 2: for a minimal prime Q of R_S through ρ, R_{S_1}/Q factors through R_{S_{1,π}} and is finite over Λ_{GSp₄,ℚ}.
A ring with nilpotent kernel onto a finite Λ-algebra need not be finite unless it is complete Noetherian local; R_{S_{1,π}} is, which is why §4.1 applies.
For F⁺ = ℚ, Λ_{GSp₄,ℚ} = O⟦x, y⟧ and finiteness means R_{S_{1,π}} is a finite O⟦x, y⟧-module.

sources.match: Asserts that R_{S_1,π} is a finite Λ_{GSp₄,F⁺}-algebra together with the reduced R = T statement.
